questions.context:
A Minor Bird
I have wished a bird would fly away,
And not sing by my house all day;
Have clapped my hands at him from the door
When it seemed as if I could bear no more.

The fault must partly have been in me.
The bird was not to blame for his key.
And of course there must be something wrong
In wanting to silence any song.
— Robert Frost
questions.stem: Choose the quote that best captures the central idea of the poem.

options.text: “A bird doesn’t sing because it has an answer. It sings because it has a song.”

options.label: B
options.text: “Like a bird singing in the rain, let grateful memories survive in times of sorrow”. – R.L. Stevenson.

options.label: C
options.text: “People are not disturbed by things but by the view they take of them”. – Epictetus.

options.label: D
options.text: “People who are innately funny are innately disturbed.” – Keenen Ivory Wayans.
